sentences.text:
THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER ORDER 41 RULE 22 OF CPC R/W SEC.173(1) OF MV ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 14.06.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.129/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE IV ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE AND MEMBER, MACT, DAKSHINA KANNADA, MANGALORE,
AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.7,27,225/- WITH INTEREST AT 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ITS REALIZATION.

THIS MFA ALONG WITH MFA CROB., COMING ON FOR FURTHER ORDERS, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

Being dissatisfied with a sum of Rs.7,27,225/-
awarded by the Tribunal as compensation for the death of Moose Byari, who was aged 63 years, the claimants are in appeal.
2. The insurer has also filed a cross-objection contending that the quantum of compensation awarded is on the higher side.
3. The occurrence of the accident and liability of the insurer to pay the compensation is not in dispute.
The Tribunal for assessing the compensation has come to the conclusion that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month.
The claimants contended that the deceased was doing arecanut business and, therefore, he was earning Rs.2,00,000/- per annum.
However, there is no evidence to substantiate these assertions.
In this view of the matter, a sum of Rs.9,000/- as determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2015 will have to be applied.

5. As the deceased was 63 years, there would be no addition of future prospects and he would be entitled for a multiplier of '7'.
6.
Since the deceased had left behind his wife and two sons apart from a daughter aged 24 years, it would be appropriate to deduct 1/4th towards 'personal expenses'.
Consequently, towards 'loss of NC: 2024:KHC:51115 dependency' the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.5,67,000/-.

4 (Rs.9,000/- - Rs.2,250/- (1/4th) = Rs.6,750/- X 12 X 7 = Rs.5,67,000/-)

sentences.text:
The claimants are the wife and children each of them would be entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/-
and it would be Rs.1,93,600/- (Rs.48,400/- X 4 members) towards 'loss of love and affection' and Rs.36,300/- under 'conventional heads'.
8. The claimants would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.32,225/- towards 'medical expenses'.
9. Consequently, the claimants is held entitled for compensation of Rs.8,29,125/- as against Rs.7,27,225/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.

However, out of the said sum, each of the children of the deceased would be entitled to withdraw a sum of NC: 2024:KHC:51115 Rs.48,400/- and the remaining amounts would be made over to the wife of the deceased.

10. However, the claimants would not be entitled for interest for the delayed period as per order dated 09.12.2024.
11.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
12. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal.
13. The appeal of the claimants is accordingly allowed in part and the cross-objection of the insurer is dismissed.

Sd/-
